messages:
maria_customer: Hey team — since the config push ~03:10 UTC our private deployment is failing to access keys. App logs show repeated KeyAccessError and a lot of TLS handshake timeouts. Can someone help?

amin_support: Sorry you're hitting this, we'll take a look. Can you paste the exact error from the Redwood agent logs and confirm this is the VPC/private install (not hosted)?

maria_customer: It's private (VPC). From the agent logs: 
```
2026-04-02T03:12:08Z ERROR keyfetch: failed to fetch key key-abc123: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = tls handshake timeout
2026-04-02T03:12:08Z DEBUG dialer: dialing kms.internal.svc.cluster.local:443 -> dial tcp: lookup kms.internal.svc.cluster.local on 169.254.169.254:53: server misbehaving
```
Also seeing intermittent "no route to host" when retries happen.

amin_support: Thanks. Two quick probes we need from the customer VMs where the agent runs: 1) DNS resolution (dig + getent) for the KMS hostname, 2) an openssl s_client to see TLS handshake and cert. Can you run these and paste outputs? Example commands: 
```
dig +short kms.internal.svc.cluster.local @<your-vpc-dns>
getent hosts kms.internal.svc.cluster.local
openssl s_client -connect kms.internal.svc.cluster.local:443 -servername kms.internal.svc.cluster.local -showcerts
```

maria_customer: Ran them, partial outputs: 
```
$ dig +short kms.internal.svc.cluster.local @10.0.0.2

$ getent hosts kms.internal.svc.cluster.local
getent: no results\n
$ openssl s_client -connect kms.internal.svc.cluster.local:443 -servername kms.internal.svc.cluster.local
connect: Connection timed out
```

tyler_infra: Looks like DNS isn't resolving to any IP from the VPC DNS and TLS connect times out -> likely egress or firewall dropping. A couple of things to check: 1) is there SNAT happening via a NAT gateway (ephemeral port exhaustion can cause random failures), 2) are the customer egress allowlist/firewall rules blocking the HSM/KMS IP range, 3) is there an internal proxy (squid/ssl-inspect) that needs client cert allowlist.

jess_prod: Also worth checking if the KMS client cert was rotated recently. If the client cert expired/rotated and the network path inspects client certs, that could cause handshake failures (or mutual TLS rejects). Can you check the agent certs at /etc/redwood/agent/certs/ and run: 
```
openssl x509 -noout -dates -in /etc/redwood/agent/certs/client.crt
```

maria_customer: cert shows expires 2026-04-02 02:59:00 UTC — oh. We had an automated rotation job that ran at 02:58 but maybe the agent never reloaded.

kms-bot: [audit] KMS handshake failed: remote_error(unknown_ca) client_cn=redwood-agent-42 ip=10.12.4.21 time=2026-04-02T03:11:59Z

amin_support: That explains the mutual TLS rejections if the old cert was still presented or intermediate CA chain not updated. But DNS still failing per dig/getent output. Two independent issues: cert rotation + DNS/egress. Let's triage in parallel.

tyler_infra: For DNS/egress — can you run a tcpdump while attempting openssl to see if SYN leaves and if there's a RST or nothing back? Example: 
```
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host <kms-host-ip> and port 443 -c 50 -w /tmp/kms-probe.pcap
```
If you don't see SYNs, the DNS or routing might be resolving to a wrong IP or the agent can't reach default gateway. Also check iptables/nft rules and conntrack table size: 
```
sudo conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
```

maria_customer: I don't have the kms-host-ip because dig returns nothing. I can try a direct NAT gateway IP though. Also we have an outbound proxy; I asked infra to check with the network team.

jess_prod: For the cert rotation: restart the agent after the cert job ran. We've seen agents keep old creds in-memory until restart. Command: 
```
sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 --no-pager
```

maria_customer: Restarted agent. Agent logs now show new client cert CN redwood-agent-43. But still failing with DNS lookup in the logs.

tyler_infra: If agent now presents valid cert, handshake errors should go away once network is fixed. For DNS, one common misconfig is the VPC DNS resolver not forwarding queries for internal.svc domains (if you use custom DNS forwarding rules). Can you check /etc/resolv.conf and VPC DHCP options? Also check whether the team's egress allowlist only permits specific destination IPs and not FQDNs — if KMS uses CNAMEs that resolve to rotating IPs that weren't added, you'll see intermittent failures.

maria_customer: /etc/resolv.conf points to the AWS-provided 10.0.0.2 (we're on GCP-like setup but using company VPC DNS). I'll ask infra to check DHCP options. Network team found the NAT gateway was at high ephemeral port usage and rotated a new NAT. They also confirmed the outbound allowlist only included a narrow set of IPs for "kms-legacy" and our new KMS cluster changed IPs after scale-up.

amin_support: That meshes with symptoms — rotation of client cert plus IP drift caused a double failure. Short-term fix: ask network team to add the current IP ranges for the KMS cluster to the egress allowlist or allow by DNS/FQDN. Also ensure NAT has enough ephemeral ports (increase NAT pool, reduce connection churn).

maria_customer: Network added the new IP prefixes and we can now resolve the kms.internal.svc.cluster.local to 10.200.5.12. After restart the agent logs show successful key fetch: 
```
2026-04-02T03:22:41Z INFO keyfetch: fetched key key-abc123 size=4096ms time=45ms
```
Service is back. Thanks.

amin_support: Awesome. For follow-up actions we'll recommend: 
- Add a post-rotate check that validates DNS resolution for critical endpoints and restarts agents if certs rotate.
- Configure NAT/egress to avoid ephemeral port exhaustion (increase pool, enable port-preserving SNAT where supported).
- Add monitoring to detect cert rotation mismatches and surface to oncall.
- Consider using a small KMS proxy (in the VPC) that handles cert rotation and stable IPs for downstream services.

jess_prod: Also adding a runbook: immediately after cert rotation, run: 
```
# verify cert
openssl x509 -noout -dates -in /etc/redwood/agent/certs/client.crt
# verify that openssl can connect
openssl s_client -connect kms.internal.svc.cluster.local:443 -servername kms.internal.svc.cluster.local
# if TLS OK but app still errors -> restart agent
sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
```

oncall-bot: Incident annotated: incident-2026-04-02-01 KMS access during cert rotation + NAT egress allowlist mismatch. Severity: SEV2. Assigned: amin_support, tyler_infra, jess_prod.

maria_customer: Thanks everyone — leaving this thread open so we can follow up on the runbook items and add a pre-rotation DNS probe to our rotation job. :thumbsup:
